questions.stem: Two triangles are congruent. This means they have:

options.text: The same perimeter but different angles
The same area but different shapes
The same angles but different side lengths

questions.explanation: Congruent triangles are identical in shape and size — all corresponding sides and angles are equal.

questions.stem: Which congruence condition requires two sides and the angle between them?
questions.explanation: SAS (Side-Angle-Side) requires two sides and the included angle between them.

questions.stem: Two right-angled triangles have equal hypotenuses and one other equal side. Which congruence condition applies?
questions.explanation: RHS (Right angle, Hypotenuse, Side) applies when two right-angled triangles share a hypotenuse and one other side.

questions.stem: Why is AAA (three equal angles) NOT a valid congruence condition?

options.text: Because the triangles might be different sizes
Because three angles cannot determine a triangle
Because it only works for right-angled triangles
Because you need at least four measurements

questions.explanation: AAA only proves the triangles are similar (same shape). They could be different sizes — like an enlargement — so AAA does not prove congruence.

questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has $AB = 7$ cm, $BC = 9$ cm, and $AC = 11$ cm. Triangle $DEF$ has $DE = 7$ cm, $EF = 9$ cm, and $DF = 11$ cm. Which condition proves they are congruent?
questions.explanation: All three pairs of corresponding sides are equal, so the triangles are congruent by SSS.

questions.stem: Two triangles have two equal angles and one equal side that is NOT between the equal angles. Can you conclude they are congruent?

options.text: No, this is not enough information

questions.explanation: AAS (Angle-Angle-Side) is a valid congruence condition. If two angles and a corresponding non-included side match, the triangles are congruent.

questions.stem: In a proof of congruent triangles using SAS, you have shown $AB = PQ$ and $BC = QR$. What else must you show?
questions.explanation: For SAS, the angle must be the included angle between the two known sides. Angle $B$ is between sides $AB$ and $BC$, and angle $Q$ is between $PQ$ and $QR$.
